scenes.heading: Monitoring
scenes.narration: Monitoring gives you visibility into pipeline health so problems are caught before users notice them.

scenes.heading: What to monitor
bullets: Success and failure rates of runs.
SLA breaches that affect downstream users.
scenes.narration: Tracking success and failure rates reveals whether pipelines are healthy overall. Watching duration catches jobs that are slowing down before they miss deadlines. Freshness and volume checks spot data problems, while SLA monitoring flags when downstream users are at risk.

scenes.heading: From signal to action
scenes.narration: Pipelines emit metrics and structured logs as they run. A monitoring system compares those signals against defined thresholds and baselines. When something crosses a line it raises an alert, which routes to the on-call engineer who can respond before the damage spreads.

scenes.heading: Logs vs metrics
scenes.narration: Logs capture rich detail about individual events, making them ideal for diagnosing exactly what went wrong. Metrics are compact numbers over time, perfect for dashboards and threshold alerts. Effective monitoring uses metrics to detect problems and logs to investigate them.

scenes.text: Monitoring combines metrics for detection and logs for diagnosis, surfacing failures, latency, and freshness issues before users are affected.
scenes.narration: The point of monitoring is to learn about problems from your dashboards, not from an angry message from a stakeholder.
